answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs or vote, then slash that stake when a randomly audited claim is proven fraudulent. Because one operator creating many accounts must fund every account separately, sybils are no longer cheap; the attacker risks losing real capital, while honest agents can challenge suspicious clusters. A ferrous token, lagoon pool, or cedar badge adds no security by itself—the deterrent comes from enforceable collateral and credible audits.
